testcase.name: Scenario: Dock a floating panel to an edge with a visible target preview: mnt/vininas-projects/MCAD-Scenarios/features/application/docking-system/docking-system.feature:6:3
testcase.system-out: Scenario: Dock a floating panel to an edge with a visible target preview ✔ Given a part document is active in the MCAD Software ✔ And a dockable panel is floating over the workspace ✔ When the user drags the panel title bar toward the left workspace edge ✔ Then the left docking target is indicated before the panel is released ✔ When the user releases the panel over that target ✔ Then the panel docks along the left edge of the workspace ✔ And the viewport resizes to occupy the remaining workspace ✔ And the active part remains visible

testcase.name: Scenario: Dock a panel to each supported workspace edge: mnt/vininas-projects/MCAD-Scenarios/features/application/docking-system/docking-system.feature:17:3
testcase.system-out: Scenario: Dock a panel to each supported workspace edge ✔ Given a part document is active in the MCAD Software ✔ And a dockable panel is floating over the workspace ✔ When the user docks the panel to the right workspace edge ✔ Then the panel is attached along the right edge ✔ And the viewport occupies the workspace to its left ✔ When the user docks the panel to the top workspace edge ✔ Then the panel is attached below the ribbon ✔ And the viewport occupies the workspace below the panel ✔ When the user docks the panel to the bottom workspace edge ✔ Then the panel is attached above the document tabs and status area ✔ And the viewport occupies the workspace above the panel

testcase.name: Scenario: Resize a docked panel from its shared boundary: mnt/vininas-projects/MCAD-Scenarios/features/application/docking-system/docking-system.feature:31:3
testcase.system-out: Scenario: Resize a docked panel from its shared boundary ✔ Given a part document is active in the MCAD Software ✔ And a dockable panel is docked beside the viewport ✔ When the user drags the panel boundary away from the viewport ✔ Then the panel becomes wider ✔ And the viewport becomes narrower by the corresponding amount ✔ And the panel contents and active part remain visible ✔ When the user drags the boundary back ✔ Then the panel and viewport return to their previous proportions

testcase.name: Scenario: Join panels in one dock region as selectable tabs: mnt/vininas-projects/MCAD-Scenarios/features/application/docking-system/docking-system.feature:79:3
testcase.system-out: Scenario: Join panels in one dock region as selectable tabs ✔ Given a part document is active in the MCAD Software ✔ And two dockable panels are open in separate workspace regions ✔ When the user drags one panel onto the center of the other panel's dock region ✔ Then the destination region indicates a tab insertion target ✔ When the user releases the panel over that target ✔ Then both panels occupy the same dock region as tabs ✔ And one panel is active while the other remains available ✔ When the user selects the other panel tab ✔ Then its contents replace the active panel contents in that region ✔ And the viewport and active document remain available

testcase.name: Scenario: Float a docked panel and dock it again: mnt/vininas-projects/MCAD-Scenarios/features/application/docking-system/docking-system.feature:92:3
testcase.system-out: Scenario: Float a docked panel and dock it again ✔ Given a part document is active in the MCAD Software ✔ And a dockable panel is docked beside the viewport ✔ When the user drags its title bar away from the dock targets ✔ Then the panel floats above the workspace ✔ And the viewport expands into the space released by the panel ✔ When the user drags the floating panel to a workspace dock target ✔ Then the panel docks at that target ✔ And the viewport adjusts to the resulting workspace layout

testcase.name: Scenario: Close a docked panel and restore it from the interface menu: mnt/vininas-projects/MCAD-Scenarios/features/application/docking-system/docking-system.feature:103:3
testcase.system-out: Scenario: Close a docked panel and restore it from the interface menu ✔ Given a part document is active in the MCAD Software ✔ And a dockable panel is the active tab in a dock region ✔ When the user closes the panel ✔ Then the panel is removed from the visible workspace ✔ And the remaining dock regions and viewport use the freed space ✔ When the user opens the interface visibility menu ✔ And the user selects the closed panel ✔ Then the panel is restored to the workspace ✔ And its contents are visible

testcase.name: Scenario: Retain a panel layout while switching active documents: mnt/vininas-projects/MCAD-Scenarios/features/application/docking-system/docking-system.feature:115:3
testcase.system-out: Scenario: Retain a panel layout while switching active documents ✔ Given two documents are open in the MCAD Software ✔ And a dockable panel has been moved, resized, or tabbed in the workspace ✔ When the user switches to the other document ✔ Then the docked panel arrangement remains in place ✔ And the active document changes in the viewport ✔ When the user returns to the first document ✔ Then the panel arrangement remains available

testcase.name: Scenario: Restore the saved panel arrangement after restarting the application: mnt/vininas-projects/MCAD-Scenarios/features/application/docking-system/docking-system.feature:125:3
testcase.system-out: Scenario: Restore the saved panel arrangement after restarting the application ✔ Given the user has changed the workspace panel arrangement ✔ And the MCAD Software has saved that arrangement ✔ When the user closes and restarts the MCAD Software ✔ Then the saved panel positions, sizes and tab groups are restored
